entry: Ran the real session store (store.mjs loadSession, saveSessionAsync, drainSessionStore; store/lifecycle-barriers.mjs bumpSessionGenerationAttempt and markSessionClosedAttempt) and manager/session-lifecycle.mjs createSession on a temp MIXDOG_DATA_DIR. The fence barriers run in a second Node process (this recorder with --child, node --import lib/determinism-preload-other-process.mjs, 120 s deadline). Did not run a turn (the provider throws if asked).
exclusions: no value is normalised; timestamps are the virtual clock (see twin.json clock) in the parent and 1700000000000 in the child process

this machine's roots (the OS temp dir -> <TMP>, the checkout process.cwd() -> <CWD>, the user home -> <HOME>; every spelling found, text after the root and its separators kept: lib/tmp-mark.mjs), in string values at barriers/fence ... messages[*].content and bpNEnvironmentContext (the stored system prompt) and every "cwd" field of a stored session. The sessions are created with cwd = the work dir <TMP>\rec-session-lifecycle (an explicit input: createSession options.cwd), so the prompt's cwd entries and git state do not depend on the checkout. The rest of the prompt (scratch dir name under rec-session-lifecycle, environment facts) is the recording machine's and stays as written

fence storedAfter is the saving process's loadSession, its live snapshot: Node admits a copy to it (store.mjs _admit: setLiveSession) before _write drops it against the generation (_dropsAgainst), so after a dropped save it holds the dropped copy while the store keeps the recorded record (durableAfter, read by another process). The core has no in-process snapshot apart from the store: storedAfter is compared only where the save landed; durableAfter is compared in every case

the place of the messages field: a session Node made in this process keeps it where createSession put it, while Node's loader assembles a stored session as its header fields followed by its messages (the transcript is the log beside the header), so a record read back after a barrier or from another process has it last. The replay's thread holds the recorded messages as one header field; each comparison places that field where the recorded record has it, every field, value and the order of all other fields compared whole
crypto.randomUUID returns 00000000-0000-4000-8000-<12-digit counter> in call order (client tokens, registration ids, server tokens, daemon session ids, call ids all come from it)
crypto.randomBytes(n) (without a callback) returns the next n values of a running byte counter modulo 256
Date.now() is 1700000000000 and performance.now() is 0 for the whole run (revisions are Date.now()*1000, queuedMs is 0) unless a case moves the virtual clock by a recorded step
process.pid is 4242 (process.kill(pid, 0) of it answers alive, as it is this process) and process.ppid is 4241; the recorded cwd is the constant "C:\\recorded\\cwd"

GLOBALS PATCHED by installDeterminism(): crypto.randomUUID, crypto.randomBytes (no-callback form), Date.now, performance.now, process.pid, process.ppid, process.kill (signal 0 of the fixed pid only). The child-process preloads (lib/determinism-preload.mjs, determinism-preload-other-process.mjs) patch crypto.randomUUID, crypto.randomBytes, Date.now and process.pid only (pid 4242, the second process 4243); they leave process.kill, performance.now and process.ppid alone

BRANCH process.pid liveness (isPidAlive / process.kill(pid, 0): src/runtime/shared/pid-liveness.mjs, ~54 files: daemon discovery in session-client, writer and process locks): the fixed pid is answered alive by the process.kill hook in the recording process; a child process preloaded with the fixed pid has no such hook, so it would judge the parent's pid dead and could steal a lock the parent held: no recorded flow has a lock held across processes (restart-prefix phases run one after the other, the lifecycle parent holds nothing while its child runs)

BRANCH process.pid equality (own-lock re-entrancy, ~33 sites such as memory-process-lock, scheduler): a recorded flow with two processes gives them different pids (4242, 4243) so they are different owners, as in production

BRANCH id collision: session ids are sess_<pid>_<n>_<Date.now()>_<randomBytes(16)>; with a fixed pid, a fixed or stepped clock and a counter for the bytes, uniqueness rests on the store's own sequence number n (nextId) and on the counters not being reset between live sessions: determinism.reset() is called only where the previous session is finished (lifecycle fresh()), and a collision would fail the save, not pass unnoticed

BRANCH ordering by time (~23 sort sites on updatedAt/createdAt): with a fixed clock timestamps tie, so a listing sorted by time falls back to insertion order; no recorded case reads a time-ordered listing of several sessions (directory listings are recorded in the OS order)

BRANCH deadlines on Date.now / performance.now (~74 performance.now sites, Date.now deadline loops such as settleTurnJournalWrites and lock timeouts): with the clock fixed they never expire inside the code under test; every wait of a recorder carries its own real-timer deadline instead, and the cases that need elapsed time move the virtual clock by a recorded step

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay: mixdog-core-session session/lifecycle_replay.rs, one test per recorded case, over the real thread store in a scratch data dir: each recorded record is a thread created under its id with the record as its header (create_with_id). Barriers: the directory's own detach and close (close.rs SessionClose::detach(id, reason, ownerClose) for detach / owner-close, SessionClose::close(id, reason) for close, re-close and agent-task-cancel), the calls thread/delete, thread/switchContext, the exit and the idle sweep make, at the recorded clock; the whole stored record (thread header) is compared before and after each step, with the generation it resolved. Fence: the late save is the thread's request thread/header/patch with expectedGeneration, which the thread drops against the header it lands on (the request SessionThreads::patch_header_fenced sends for the delegation rebind, agent_send_world.rs ThreadHeaders); its change is the late record's fields that differ from the stored one; the outcome (saved / dropped), the whole durableAfter record and, for a save that landed, the whole storedAfter record are compared.
